text: Researchers used names indicate race various experimental tasks surveys, conjoint experiments, correspondence experiments. , researchers must consider least following three factors: Choose names vary race remain constant across perceived attributes, choose names vary race perceived attributes. Use one several names increase reliability. Use names indicate differences citizenship, education, income within across races explore. title: Validated names for experimental studies
text: select_names() function helps choose validated names intended signal particular race using race argument. options available argument : Asian, Black, Hispanic, White. output data dataframe nine columns: first (first name), last = last name, w.asian = westernized Asian name (1 = yes, 0 = ), name (full name), identity (name’s intended race), mean_correct = percentage name’s intended race correctly perceived (0-1), avg_income = average perceived income level (1-5), avg_education = average perceived education level (1-5), avg_citizenship = percentage perceived citizenship status (0-1). can change threshold level names correctly perceived using pct_correct argument. default value argument 0.8. can also change number names selected using n_names argument. default value argument 5. names selected randomly. Rather using random sampling, possible select names ordering according chosen variable. done specifying order_by_var argument. values available : pct_correct = percentage name’s intended race correctly perceived, avg_income = average perceived income level, avg_education = average perceived education level, avg_citizenship = percentage perceived citizenship status. Finally, like select names racial groups, use select_nams_all() instead select_names(). Note select_names_all() race argument, arguments identical.
code: asian_names <- select_names(race = "Asian") # Asian signalling names   asian_names   #>   first last  w.asian name      identity       mean_correct avg_income avg_education avg_citizenship #>   <chr> <chr>   <dbl> <chr>     <fct>            <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl>   <dbl> #> 1 Dan   Yang        1 Dan Yang  Asian or Paci…   0.848    2.09    2.55   0.773 #> 2 Hong  Pham        0 Hong Pham Asian or Paci…   0.826    1.94    2.28   0.465 #> 3 May   Chen        1 May Chen  Asian or Paci…   0.878    2.07    2.37   0.789 #> 4 Hong  Le          0 Hong Le   Asian or Paci…   0.816    1.97    2.42   0.539 #> 5 Wei   Le          0 Wei Le    Asian or Paci…   0.806    1.93    2.18   0.418 # change the threshold level of the names to be correctly perceived from 0.8 (the default value) to 0.7  high_thres_names <- select_names(race = "Asian", pct_correct = 0.7) # change the number of the names to be selected from 5 (the default value) to 10   greater_n_names <- select_names(race = "Asian", n_names = 10) top_correct_names <- select_names(race = "Asian", order_by = "pct_correct") all_race_names <- select_names_all()
